summary:
The headline signal today is full consensus on MIL over ATL, the slate's strongest average delta (R1 +1.95, R2 +1.87, R3 +2.13, R4 +1.83), and it lines up perfectly with the model's best team-when-liked profile: MIL sits 26-15 (63%, n=41) with a strong-play mark of 15-8 (+5.0u). Bullpen is running hot across the board right now — R1, R2 and R3 all show bullpen at 54% over the last 14 days (101-87, n=188) versus a season baseline around 51%, and with Sale on the mound against a Misiorowski-led Brewers pen, this is exactly the kind of matchup where a hot bullpen category and a consensus team pick stack. BOS is another green light: all four ratings agree on Boston (R1-R3 clustered 0.92-1.01, R4 highest at +1.27), and BOS-when-picked is money at 76% (29-9, n=38) with strong plays running +15.0u. PHI also gets unanimous support (0.53-1.05 range) and sits at a healthy 59% (17-12) with +2.0u on strong plays — a lower-conviction but still trustworthy side.

Fade spots worth flagging: CHC @ SEA is unanimous the other way, all four ratings against Chicago (-0.52 to -0.76), which matters since CHC is otherwise 70% (19-8) when picked — today's road spot with Boyd on the mound is the exception, not the trend, so respect the model's read here rather than the team's overall profile. SP remains the weak link leaguewide, sitting at just 46% over the last 14 days for R1/R2 (87-101, n=188) and only 48% for R3, so don't lean heavily on starter-driven edges alone — that's relevant on the thinner consensus plays like ARI (+0.42 to +0.96) and LAD (+0.45 to +1.04), where the pitching matchups (Rodriguez, Yamamoto) look strong on paper but the model's SP category hasn't been backing that up lately. Split-decision games — TBR/BAL, MIN/SDP, WSN/MIA, TOR/NYY, ATH/HOU — are where R4's small sample (9 games, 78% on trends/runs) diverges from the veteran three ratings; treat those as pass or small-stake spots until R4's sample grows.
